   def pr_of_head(repo: str, head: str) -> tuple[str, str]:                                                                                                                                                
       """(number, author) of the open pull request whose head is `head`, or ("", "").                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       ci-success hands this gate the pull request in the environment (PR_NUMBER/PR_BODY/                                                                                                                  
       PR_AUTHOR, .github/workflows/ci.yml), because a pull request event carries it. The Greenlane                                                                                                        
       runs the same gate one stage earlier, on a LANE -- a branch -- and exports none of it                                                                                                               
       (greenlane/github.py::unclaimed passes only GITHUB_REPOSITORY). That was invisible while                                                                                                            
       every lane declared its two trailers in a commit message, and became a false `no live claim`                                                                                                        
       the moment one declared them in its pull request body -- which AGENTS.md §5 rule 5 allows                                                                                                           
       ("in a commit message (or the PR body)"), which judge() reads (it appends the body), and                                                                                                            
       which both #6202 and #6198 did.                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Measured 2026-10-15 against a clean origin/main, greenlane holding both with                                                                                                                        
       `no live claim: no `Claim: <owner>/<repo>#<n>` line` while both were green and mergeable:                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
           PR_NUMBER unset  -> FAIL  claim-gate  no `Claim: <owner>/<repo>#<n>` line                                                                                                                       
           PR_NUMBER=6202   -> ok    claim-gate  no other live agent holds these files                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Asking GitHub which pull request this sha is the head of supplies the same fact CI is handed,                                                                                                       
       so the lane stage and the queue cannot answer the same question differently.                                                                                                                        
       """                                                                                                                                                                                                 
       key = (repo, head)                                                                                                                                                                                  
       if key not in _PRS:                                                                                                                                                                                 
           _PRS[key] = ("", "")                                                                                                                                                                            
           try:                                                                                                                                                                                            
               p = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603, S607 -- fixed argv, no shell                                                                                                                             
                   ["gh", "api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{head}/pulls"],                                                                                                                                    
                   capture_output=True,                                                                                                                                                                    
                   text=True,                                                                                                                                                                              
                   timeout=30,                                                                                                                                                                             
               )                                                                                                                                                                                           
               found = json.loads(p.stdout or "[]") if p.returncode == 0 else []                                                                                                                           
           except Exception:                                                                                                                                                                               
               found = []                                                                                                                                                                                  
           for pr in found if isinstance(found, list) else []:                                                                                                                                             
               if pr.get("state") == "open":                                                                                                                                                               
                   _PRS[key] = (                                                                                                                                                                           
                       str(pr.get("number", "")),                                                                                                                                                          
                       ((pr.get("user") or {}).get("login") or ""),                                                                                                                                        
                   )                                                                                                                                                                                       
                   break                                                                                                                                                                                   
       return _PRS[key]                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
   def pr_context(repo: str, head: str) -> tuple[str, str]:                                                                                                                                                
       """The pull request this run judges: CI's environment first, GitHub's answer second.                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       CI sets both variables, so it pays nothing for this. The lane stage sets neither, which is                                                                                                          
       the whole defect -- it now asks which pull request this sha is the head of.                                                                                                                         
       """                                                                                                                                                                                                 
       num = os.environ.get("PR_NUMBER", "")                                                                                                                                                               
       author = os.environ.get("PR_AUTHOR", "")                                                                                                                                                            
       if num and author:                                                                                                                                                                                  
           return num, author                                                                                                                                                                              
       found_num, found_author = pr_of_head(repo, head)                                                                                                                                                    
       return num or found_num, author or found_author                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
   def lane_body(repo: str, lane_head: str, squash: str) -> str:                                                                                                                                           
       """The body of the pull request a landed lane came from, or "".                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       judge()'s lane path reads the LANE BRANCH's commit messages (lane_text), so a lane whose two                                                                                                        
       trailers live in its pull request body was refused here even after the lane stage admitted it                                                                                                       
       -- the same blindness, one stage later. Try the head the trailer names, then the squash the                                                                                                         
       batch carries: whichever GitHub still associates with the pull request."""                                                                                                                          
       for sha in (lane_head, squash):                                                                                                                                                                     
           num, _ = pr_of_head(repo, sha)                                                                                                                                                                  
           if num:                                                                                                                                                                                         
               return live_body(repo, num)                                                                                                                                                                 
       return ""                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
   def live_body(repo: str, num: str = "") -> str:                                                                                                                                                         
       """The PR body as it is now, not as the opening-day event snapshot carried it (idp#5758:                                                                                                            
       a re-run judges github.event.pull_request.body from the original event, so a trailer fix                                                                                                            
       in the body stayed invisible and the gate failed identically). Falls back to the snapshot                                                                                                           
       when there is no PR number or the fetch fails -- CI still runs the same gate."""                                                                                                                    
       num = num or os.environ.get("PR_NUMBER", "")                                                                                                                                                        
       if not num:                                                                                                                                                                                         
           return os.environ.get("PR_BODY", "")                                                                                                                                                            
 ```

       restarted the 24 hours, and a lane could sit in the queue for weeks, head unmoved...                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       The age of a commit cannot be re-stamped: `git` records the author date when the commit is                                                                                                          
       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the                                                                                                            
       committer date moves. So the clock is read from the work, and nothing the engine does to the                                                                                                        
       ref (rebase, re-push, re-observe) can move it. A lane that cannot be read (the commit object                                                                                                        
       is not local) is not retired: an unknown age is not a reason to park work (I4).

       """A lane whose work is older than RETIRE_AFTER_MIN is parked (idp#5953).                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Measured 2026-10-16 on refs/greenlane/state: 32 of 43 lanes carried a head commit 24h..17d

       clock was the defect: it was stamped into the state file when the engine first *saw* a head,                                                                                                        
       so every re-observation (a state wipe, a prune, a lost tick, `ls-remote` missing a ref)                                                                                                             
       restarted the 24 hours, and a lane could sit in the queue for weeks, head unmoved...                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       The age of a commit cannot be re-stamped: `git` records the author date when the commit is                                                                                                          
       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the                                                                                                            
       committer date moves. So the clock is read from the work, and nothing the engine does to the                                                                                                        
       ref (rebase, re-push, re-observe) can move it. A lane that cannot be read (the commit object                                                                                                        
       is not local) is not retired: an unknown age is not a reason to park work (I4).                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Lanes under test right now are skipped...                                                                                                                                                           
       """                                                                                                                                                                                                 
       now = self.b.now()                                                                                                                                                                                  
       testing = {m[0] for m in (self.s.batch.members if self.s.batch else [])}                                                                                                                            
       for name in list(self.s.lanes):                                                                                                                                                                     
           lane = self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                       
           if name in testing:

           self.b.report(name, lane.head, RED, reason)                                                                                                                                                     
           del self.s.lanes[name]

       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the

       """A lane whose work is older than RETIRE_AFTER_MIN is parked (idp#5953).

       clock was the defect: it was stamped into the state file when the engine first *saw* a head,                                                                                                        
       so every re-observation (a state wipe, a prune, a lost tick, `ls-remote` missing a ref)                                                                                                             
       restarted the 24 hours, and a lane could sit in the queue for weeks, head unmoved...                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       The age of a commit cannot be re-stamped: `git` records the author date when the commit is                                                                                                          
       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the                                                                                                            
       committer date moves. So the clock is read from the work, and nothing the engine does to the                                                                                                        
       ref (rebase, re-push, re-observe) can move it. A lane that cannot be read (the commit object                                                                                                        
       is not local) is not retired: an unknown age is not a reason to park work (I4).

       for name in list(self.s.lanes):                                                                                                                                                                     
           lane = self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                       
           if name in testing:

           self.b.report(name, lane.head, RED, reason)                                                                                                                                                     
           del self.s.lanes[name]

   def _retire_stale_lanes(self) -> None:                                                                                                                                                                  
       """A lane whose work is older than RETIRE_AFTER_MIN is parked (idp#5953).                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Measured 2026-10-16 on refs/greenlane/state: 32 of 43 lanes carried a head commit 24h..17d                                                                                                          
       old -- median 8.8 days -- while the engine's own clock said none of them was a day old. The                                                                                                         
       clock was the defect: it was stamped into the state file when the engine first *saw* a head,                                                                                                        
       so every re-observation (a state wipe, a prune, a lost tick, `ls-remote` missing a ref)                                                                                                             
       restarted the 24 hours, and a lane could sit in the queue for weeks, head unmoved...                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       The age of a commit cannot be re-stamped: `git` records the author date when the commit is                                                                                                          
       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the                                                                                                            
       committer date moves. So the clock is read from the work, and nothing the engine does to the                                                                                                        
       ref (rebase, re-push, re-observe) can move it. A lane that cannot be read (the commit object                                                                                                        
       is not local) is not retired: an unknown age is not a reason to park work (I4).                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Lanes under test right now are skipped...                                                                                                                                                           
       """                                                                                                                                                                                                 
       now = self.b.now()                                                                                                                                                                                  
       testing = {m[0] for m in (self.s.batch.members if self.s.batch else [])}                                                                                                                            
       for name in list(self.s.lanes):                                                                                                                                                                     
           lane = self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                       
           if name in testing:                                                                                                                                                                             
               continue                                                                                                                                                                                    
           age = self.b.work_age(lane.head)                                                                                                                                                                
           if age is None or age < RETIRE_AFTER_MIN:                                                                                                                                                       
               continue                                                                                                                                                                                    
           days = age / (60 * 24)

           self.s.retired[name] = lane.head                                                                                                                                                                
           self.b.report(name, lane.head, RED, reason)                                                                                                                                                     
           del self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                          
           self.log.append(f"retired {name}: {reason}")

       """A lane whose work is older than RETIRE_AFTER_MIN is parked (idp#5953).                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Measured 2026-10-16 on refs/greenlane/state: 32 of 43 lanes carried a head commit 24h..17d                                                                                                          
       old -- median 8.8 days -- while the engine's own clock said none of them was a day old. The                                                                                                         
       clock was the defect: it was stamped into the state file when the engine first *saw* a head,                                                                                                        
       so every re-observation (a state wipe, a prune, a lost tick, `ls-remote` missing a ref)                                                                                                             
       restarted the 24 hours, and a lane could sit in the queue for weeks, head unmoved...                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       The age of a commit cannot be re-stamped: `git` records the author date when the commit is                                                                                                          
       made, and a rebase -- including the engine's own stale-refresh -- preserves it while the                                                                                                            
       committer date moves. So the clock is read from the work, and nothing the engine does to the                                                                                                        
       ref (rebase, re-push, re-observe) can move it. A lane that cannot be read (the commit object                                                                                                        
       is not local) is not retired: an unknown age is not a reason to park work (I4).                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
       Lanes under test right now are skipped...                                                                                                                                                           
       """

       testing = {m[0] for m in (self.s.batch.members if self.s.batch else [])}                                                                                                                            
       for name in list(self.s.lanes):                                                                                                                                                                     
           lane = self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                       
           if name in testing:                                                                                                                                                                             
               continue                                                                                                                                                                                    
           age = self.b.work_age(lane.head)                                                                                                                                                                
           if age is None or age < RETIRE_AFTER_MIN:                                                                                                                                                       
               continue                                                                                                                                                                                    
           days = age / (60 * 24)                                                                                                                                                                          
           reason = f"refused: retired, this lane head is {days:.0f} days old"                                                                                                                             
           self.s.retired[name] = lane.head                                                                                                                                                                
           self.b.report(name, lane.head, RED, reason)                                                                                                                                                     
           del self.s.lanes[name]                                                                                                                                                                          
           self.log.append(f"retired {name}: {reason}")

## P0 — Kill the cold-start (the actual root cause)

`/voice/say` hanging 20s+ then serving 1.35s warm is a lazy provider init. Elite fix, three layers:

1. **Eager warmup + readiness gate** — at fleetview start, run one synthetic synth before binding/announcing healthy. The service isn't "up" until it can actually speak. No user ever sees the cold load again.
2. **Keep-alive** — self-hosted healthcheck (healthchecks.io, free tier) hits `/voice/say` every 10–15 min so the engine never goes cold. ~15 machine-minutes.
3. **Bounded client wait + circuit breaker** — face client waits max 4s for a clause buffer; on miss, fast-fallback with `podVoiceRestsUntil` (you already have this pattern — tighten it). A hanging upstream must cost 4s, never 20s+.

## P0 — One voice path, streaming only

Two parallel voice stacks (old hook vs. router, 0 turns on router) is how rot happens. Elite standard:

- Write the **adapter** so FacePage mounts `useVoiceRouter` (fields `checking/micRecoveryUrl/heard/reply` mapped). SLO: **first audio < 2.5s p95**.
- Delete `useEstateVoice`'s old path from FacePage once the adapter is green — one path, one place to fix, forever.
- Ship behind a flag so you can roll back without redeploying.

## P1 — The mouth never freezes again

This is your brand promise ("delightful"), so make it structural: **every speech path drives `clauseSink`**. Real TTS buffer → real lipsync. Device-voice fallback → procedural viseme envelope for the clause duration. Frozen mouth becomes *unreachable by construction*, not "shouldn't happen."

## P1 — Mic gate + captions

- **Optimistic start**: tap begins streaming immediately; `/voice/voices` resolves in background. First command is never hostage to a check.
- **Caption clamp**: `-webkit-line-clamp: 3` + `max-height` on the reply pill; on small viewports captions sit *below* the face, never over it.

## P2 — Hardering

- **Router flapping** (PID changed mid-session): supervise under launchd with `KeepAlive`, alert on restart. Silent process death is an incident, not a shrug.
- **Surface truth**: the archaeology burned ~20 probes because nobody documented where the face is served. One line in `crew/STATE.md` §5 ends that permanently.

## The "elite" is in the verification

- One ticket, one claim, `lane/fix/face-voice-ux` off main — your governance rules, followed exactly.
- **Tests that execute**: warm-say contract test (<4s), mocked-hang timeout test, mouth-driven-on-fallback test, caption-clamp test, adapter shape test.
- **Dashboard before closure**: turn latency p50/p95, device-fallback rate, cold-start count. If you can't see it degrade, it will degrade silently.

**Estimate**: ~4–6 machine-hours of implementation + 1–2 for tests/CI. Sequencing: P0 cold-start first (it fixes latency + mouth for real users today), then the adapter swap, then P1 polish.

new work spec and code # Run-To-Completion System — Full Spec (BDD)

Status: PROPOSED — founder executes, agents propose. No paid infra, no daemons.
Definition of done: `pytest features/` is green and the gate has run 7 shadow
days clean, then founder flips ENFORCE.

## 1. Scope

Agents drive tasks to exactly one terminal state — `done` (operational, proven)
or `failed` (all alternates exhausted, evidenced) — with at most one
founder-facing message per task, and only when a decision is required.

Non-goals: agent-to-agent chat, progress reporting, notifications to founder
inbox, anything requiring paid services.

## 2. Conventions

- State root: `~/.fortress/state/<repo>/<task-id>.yaml` (outside all repos —
worktrees get destroyed; state must not).
- Archive: `~/.fortress/state/archive/` after 48h at terminal state.
- Proof bundles: committed to `docs/reports/<task-id>-<date>.md` (repo).
- Heartbeat: self-hosted healthchecks.io, API base `$HC`, key `$HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY`.
- Every founder-facing message carries header `Task: <task-id>`.
- Estimates in machine-hours only.
- Work happens only in the task's own `git worktree`, absolute paths, `git -C`.

## 3. Features (Gherkin — each scenario is an executable test)

### F1 — Run-to-completion messaging

Feature: Run-to-completion messaging
Agents send zero chat messages while working; at most one, and only as a
formatted decision request, before terminal state.

Scenario: Silent progress
Given agent "codex-7" owns task "idp#6603"
And the task is not terminal and no decision is pending
When 60 machine-minutes of work pass
Then the agent sent 0 chat messages

Scenario: Reversible blocker self-resolves
Given the primary path hits a reversible in-lane blocker
When the agent exhausts the primary path
Then it tries alternate paths B and C
And it sends 0 decision messages

Scenario: Decision request format
Given every alternate path is exhausted
When the agent requests a decision
Then the message starts with "Task: idp#6603"
And it contains exactly: what happened (<=2 lines), the decision (<=1 line),
recommended action plus exact command, and the default on silence
And decision_pending is recorded in the state file

Scenario: Reversible decision auto-resolves
Given decision_pending.reversible is true
And asked_at is 2 machine-hours in the past with no founder reply
When the agent checks the state file
Then it executes the recommendation
And appends the action to attempts

Scenario: Irreversible decision parks
Given decision_pending.reversible is false
When no founder reply arrives
Then the agent stops work on this task and sends no further messages
And the task appears on the founder's parked-decisions dashboard view

Scenario: Estimate breach surfaces
Given elapsed_hours is greater than 2 times estimate_hours
Then the agent must send one decision message with a revised estimate
And this message never counts against the message budget

### F2 — Task claim and state file

Scenario: Claim before work
When an agent starts task "idp#6603"
Then it writes the state file before running any other command
And the file records: agent, worktree (absolute), goal, acceptance,
estimate_hours, heartbeat slug, status "working", next_step

Scenario: Live claim blocks adoption
Given a state file with a fresh heartbeat (< 20 min old)
When a second agent attempts the same task
Then it stops and selects different work
And it sends no message

Scenario: Stale claim is adoptable
Given a state file whose heartbeat is silent for more than 20 minutes
When a second agent attempts the same task
Then it appends "adopted from <agent> at <ts>" to attempts
And resumes from next_step with no founder message

### F3 — Heartbeat liveness

Scenario: Claim creates check
When an agent claims a task
Then a healthchecks check exists with channels empty and timeout 600, grace 600
And the agent pings /start

Scenario: Activity pings
Given a working task
When the agent completes a command batch
Then it pings the check before starting the next batch
And pings piggyback on activity — no cron, no daemon

Scenario: Death is visible
Given a task with no ping for more than 20 minutes
Then the check shows DOWN on the dashboard
And zero notifications fire

### F4 — Terminal state and proof

Scenario: Done requires proof
When an agent marks a task done
Then proof contains the verification command and observed output
And the proof bundle is committed under docs/reports/

Scenario: Failed requires exhaustion evidence
When an agent marks a task failed
Then attempts show every alternate path tried and its result
And remaining risk is stated in one line

Scenario: Gate drops unproven terminal claims
Given a terminal message without a proof bundle
Then the gate rejects it regardless of mode

### F5 — Message-count gate

Scenario: Shadow mode logs
Given GATE_MODE=shadow
When a second non-decision message arrives for a task header
Then the violation is logged with task id, agent, and snippet
And the message is delivered

Scenario: Enforce mode blocks
Given GATE_MODE=enforce
When a second non-decision message arrives for a task header
Then the message is rejected with "Protocol F1: run to completion"
And decision-request, estimate-breach, and terminal messages always pass

### F6 — Workspace isolation

Scenario: Own worktree only
Given an agent owns task "idp#6603" with worktree /…/idp-<task>
When it runs any git command
Then it uses git -C with the absolute worktree path

Scenario: Foreign checkout is a hard stop
Given a command would modify a checkout owned by another lane
Then the agent stops and sends one irreversible-decision message
And makes no attempt to repair without approval

## 4. State file schema (normative)

task, repo, lane, worktree, status, goal, acceptance, claim{agent,since},
estimate_hours, elapsed_hours, heartbeat, attempts[]{at,did,result,evidence},
blockers[], next_step, decision_pending{question,recommendation,reversible,
asked_at,auto_resolve_at}, proof.

## 5. Build plan (machine-hours)

| Phase | Deliverable | Hours | Tooling (free) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | AGENTS.md protocol section referencing this spec | 0.5 | founder executes |
| P1 | Test harness: features/*.feature + pytest-bdd steps | 1.0 | python3, pytest, pytest-bdd |
| P2 | State lib: claim/adopt/append/terminal transitions | 2.0 | python stdlib + PyYAML |
| P3 | Heartbeat wrapper hc.sh (claim/ping/start/fail/log) | 1.0 | curl, healthchecks API |
| P4 | Gate: header parse, per-task counter, shadow log | 2.0 | python stdlib |
| P5 | Proof-bundle lint wired into gate | 1.0 | python stdlib |
| — | Total | 7.5 |  |

## 6. Rollout checkpoints (founder go required)

1. Set HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY + HC on the Mac.
2. P1–P3 pass locally.
3. Gate runs GATE_MODE=shadow for 7 days; founder reviews violation log.
4. Founder flips GATE_MODE=enforce.
5. Weekly: archive sweep + parked-decisions review (dashboard, not inbox).

See rtc-bdd-spec.md section 6 for the full checklist. # AGENTS.md — Run-To-Completion Protocol (hard rule, all agents)

Full spec: `rtc-bdd-spec.md`. Reference implementation: `fortress-rtc/`.
Violation after the enforce date = removal from crew.

1. Drive every task to ONE terminal state: `done` (operational + proven) or
`failed` (all alternates exhausted + evidenced). No third state.
2. NEVER send progress updates. Silence means working. Claim first:
`rtc/state.py claim(...)`, then ping `rtc/heartbeat.sh ping <repo> <task>`
after every command batch. No daemon, no cron — piggyback only.
3. You may interrupt the founder ONLY for a decision, with `Task: <id>` header,
`DECISION:` prefix, <=2 lines what happened, the decision, your
recommendation + exact command, and the default on silence.
4. `reversible: true` decisions auto-execute your recommendation after 2
machine-hours of silence (logged). `false` parks; do not nag.
5. Inside your lane and reversible = just do it, report at terminal state.
Irreversible or outside your lane = stop and ask FIRST.
6. Blockers: exhaust alternates before escalating. `blocked` is not terminal
unless every route has an evidence entry in `attempts`.
7. `elapsed > 2x estimate` -> send ONE `ESTIMATE:` message with a revised
estimate. Never "days"/"weeks"; machine-hours only.
8. Terminal messages carry `DONE:` or `FAILED:` plus a mandatory `Proof:` line
(command + observed output). Unproven terminal claims are dropped.
9. Work only in your own `git worktree`, absolute paths, `git -C`. Touching
another lane's checkout = hard stop + one irreversible-decision message.
10. Messages route through the gate. DECISION/ESTIMATE/proven-terminal are
exempt; everything else is budgeted to one per task. state.py
"""rtc.state -- task state files for the Run-To-Completion protocol.

One YAML file per task, OUTSIDE every repo:
    ~/.fortress/state/<repo>/<task-id>.yaml
Sidecars:
    <task-id>.ping    touched by heartbeat.sh on every ping (liveness, no network)
    <task-id>.hcuuid  healthchecks ping uuid (written at claim)

All timestamps are epoch seconds (float). Pass `now` explicitly in tests.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

STATUS_WORKING = "working"
STATUS_BLOCKED = "blocked"
STATUS_DONE = "done"
STATUS_FAILED = "failed"

DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS = 1200       # 2x healthchecks grace of 600s
DEFAULT_AUTO_RESOLVE_HOURS = 2.0   # reversible decisions auto-resolve
ESTIMATE_BREACH_FACTOR = 2.0


class ClaimError(Exception):
    """Raised when a live claim blocks the operation."""


class ProofError(Exception):
    """Raised when a terminal transition lacks required proof."""


def _iso(ts: float) -> str:
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat()


def state_root(root: str | os.PathLike | None = None) -> Path:
    if root is not None:
        return Path(root)
    env = os.environ.get("RTC_STATE_ROOT")
    if env:
        return Path(env)
    return Path.home() / ".fortress" / "state"


def state_path(repo: str, task: str, root=None) -> Path:
    return state_root(root) / repo / f"{task}.yaml"


def ping_path(repo: str, task: str, root=None) -> Path:
    return state_root(root) / repo / f"{task}.ping"


def uuid_path(repo: str, task: str, root=None) -> Path:
    return state_root(root) / repo / f"{task}.hcuuid"


def load(repo: str, task: str, root=None) -> dict:
    p = state_path(repo, task, root)
    with open(p) as fh:
        return yaml.safe_load(fh)


def save(state: dict, root=None) -> None:
    p = state_path(state["repo"], state["task"], root)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".tmp")
    with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
        yaml.safe_dump(state, fh, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)
    os.replace(tmp, p)


def last_ping(repo: str, task: str, root=None) -> float | None:
    """Most recent activity ping, from the local sidecar (no network)."""
    p = ping_path(repo, task, root)
    try:
        return p.stat().st_mtime
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- transitions

def blank(task, repo, agent, worktree, goal, acceptance, estimate_hours,
          heartbeat, now=None) -> dict:
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    return {
        "task": task,
        "repo": repo,
        "lane": f"lane/{task}",
        "worktree": str(worktree),
        "status": STATUS_WORKING,
        "goal": goal,
        "acceptance": acceptance,
        "claim": {"agent": agent, "since": now},
        "estimate_hours": float(estimate_hours),
        "grace_seconds": DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS,
        "heartbeat": heartbeat,
        "attempts": [],
        "blockers": [],
        "next_step": "",
        "decision_pending": None,
        "proof": None,
    }


def claim(repo, task, agent, worktree, goal, acceptance, estimate_hours,
          heartbeat, now=None, root=None) -> dict:
    """Create a fresh claim. Refuses if ANY state file already exists --
    stale claims must be adopted explicitly via adopt()."""
    if state_path(repo, task, root).exists():
        raise ClaimError(f"{task}: state file exists; use adopt() if claim is dead")
    st = blank(task, repo, agent, worktree, goal, acceptance,
               estimate_hours, heartbeat, now)
    save(st, root)
    return st


def claim_is_live(state: dict, now=None, root=None) -> bool:
    """True while the owner is verifiably alive: working/blocked and the
    most recent activity (ping sidecar, else claim time) is within grace."""
    if state["status"] in (STATUS_DONE, STATUS_FAILED):
        return False
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    ref = last_ping(state["repo"], state["task"], root)
    if ref is None:
        ref = float(state["claim"]["since"])
    return (now - ref) < float(state.get("grace_seconds", DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS))


def adopt(repo, task, new_agent, now=None, root=None) -> dict:
    """Take over a dead claim. No founder message; resume from next_step."""
    st = load(repo, task, root)
    if claim_is_live(st, now, root):
        raise ClaimError(f"{task}: claim held by {st['claim']['agent']} is live")
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    old = st["claim"]["agent"]
    st["attempts"].append({
        "at": _iso(now),
        "did": f"adopted from {old}",
        "result": "pass",
        "evidence": None,
    })
    st["claim"] = {"agent": new_agent, "since": now}
    st["status"] = STATUS_WORKING
    save(st, root)
    return st


def append_attempt(state, did, result, evidence=None, now=None) -> dict:
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    state["attempts"].append({
        "at": _iso(now), "did": did, "result": result, "evidence": evidence,
    })
    return state


def set_next_step(state, step: str) -> dict:
    state["next_step"] = step
    return state


def request_decision(state, question, recommendation, reversible,
                     now=None, auto_hours=DEFAULT_AUTO_RESOLVE_HOURS) -> dict:
    """Record a decision request. Caller sends the ONE formatted message."""
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    state["decision_pending"] = {
        "question": question,
        "recommendation": recommendation,
        "reversible": bool(reversible),
        "asked_at": now,
        "auto_resolve_at": (now + auto_hours * 3600) if reversible else None,
    }
    state["status"] = STATUS_BLOCKED
    return state


def decision_due(state, now=None) -> bool:
    """True if a reversible decision went unanswered past its deadline."""
    dp = state.get("decision_pending")
    if not dp or not dp.get("reversible"):
        return False
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    return now >= float(dp["auto_resolve_at"])


def resolve_decision(state, now=None) -> dict:
    """Execute the recommendation after silence. Logged, then keep working."""
    dp = state["decision_pending"]
    append_attempt(state, f"auto-resolved decision: {dp['recommendation']}",
                   "pass", now=now)
    state["decision_pending"] = None
    state["status"] = STATUS_WORKING
    return state


def elapsed_hours(state, now=None) -> float:
    now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
    return (now - float(state["claim"]["since"])) / 3600.0


def estimate_breached(state, now=None) -> bool:
    return elapsed_hours(state, now) > ESTIMATE_BREACH_FACTOR * float(
        state["estimate_hours"])


def mark_done(state, proof_cmd, proof_output, evidence_path=None,
              now=None, root=None) -> dict:
    """Terminal: operational AND proven. Proof is mandatory."""
    if not proof_cmd or not proof_output:
        raise ProofError("done requires proof_cmd and observed proof_output")
    append_attempt(state, f"verified: {proof_cmd}", "pass",
                   evidence_path, now=now)
    state["proof"] = {
        "cmd": proof_cmd,
        "output": proof_output,
        "evidence": evidence_path,
    }
    state["status"] = STATUS_DONE
    save(state, root)
    return state


def mark_failed(state, risk_line, now=None, root=None) -> dict:
    """Terminal: every alternate exhausted. Evidence (attempts) mandatory."""
    if not state.get("attempts"):
        raise ProofError("failed requires at least one attempt as evidence")
    append_attempt(state, f"FAILED. remaining risk: {risk_line}", "fail",
                   now=now)
    state["status"] = STATUS_FAILED
    save(state, root)
    return state """rtc.gate -- message-count gate + proof lint.

Modes:
  shadow  violations are logged (JSONL) but messages are delivered
  enforce violations are rejected; only the first non-exempt message per
          (agent, task) passes

Every founder-facing message MUST start with a header line:
    Task: <task-id>

Message kinds (prefix conventions, exempt from the count):
  DECISION:   needs a founder decision (F1)
  ESTIMATE:   elapsed > 2x estimate (F1; mandatory escalation)
  DONE:/FAILED: terminal state -- must contain a `Proof:` line or are
          rejected in BOTH modes (F4)
Anything else is a status message and counts against the budget.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import time
from pathlib import Path

HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^Task:\s*(\S+)", re.M)
DECISION_RE = re.compile(r"^DECISION:", re.M)
ESTIMATE_RE = re.compile(r"^ESTIMATE:", re.M)
TERMINAL_RE = re.compile(r"^(DONE:|FAILED:)", re.M)
PROOF_RE = re.compile(r"^Proof:", re.M)

EXEMPT = {"decision", "estimate_breach", "terminal"}
MODES = ("shadow", "enforce")


def classify(message: str) -> str:
    if DECISION_RE.search(message):
        return "decision"
    if ESTIMATE_RE.search(message):
        return "estimate_breach"
    if TERMINAL_RE.search(message):
        return "terminal"
    return "status"


class Gate:
    def __init__(self, mode: str = "shadow", log_path=None):
        if mode not in MODES:
            raise ValueError(f"mode must be one of {MODES}")
        self.mode = mode
        self._counts: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
        self.log_path = Path(log_path) if log_path else None

    def _log(self, record: dict) -> None:
        if not self.log_path:
            return
        self.log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(self.log_path, "a") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")

    def process(self, agent: str, message: str, now=None) -> dict:
        """Route one message. Returns {result: deliver|reject, reason}."""
        now = time.time() if now is None else float(now)
        m = HEADER_RE.search(message)
        task = m.group(1) if m else "<missing-header>"
        kind = classify(message)

        if not m:
            rec = {"ts": now, "agent": agent, "task": task,
                   "kind": kind, "action": "reject", "reason": "missing Task header"}
            self._log(rec)
            return {"result": "reject" if self.mode == "enforce" else "deliver",
                    "reason": "missing Task header"}

        if kind == "terminal" and not PROOF_RE.search(message):
            # F4: unproven terminal claims are dropped regardless of mode.
            rec = {"ts": now, "agent": agent, "task": task, "kind": kind,
                   "action": "reject", "reason": "terminal without Proof:"}
            self._log(rec)
            return {"result": "reject", "reason": "terminal without Proof:"}

        if kind in EXEMPT:
            return {"result": "deliver", "reason": f"exempt:{kind}"}

        key = (agent, task)
        self._counts[key] = self._counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        if self._counts[key] == 1:
            return {"result": "deliver", "reason": "first status message allowed"}

# rtc heartbeat -- liveness pings piggybacked on agent activity. No daemon.
#
# Usage:
#   heartbeat.sh claim  <repo> <task> <check-name>
#   heartbeat.sh start  <repo> <task>
#   heartbeat.sh ping   <repo> <task>
#   heartbeat.sh fail   <repo> <task> [message]
#   heartbeat.sh log    <repo> <task> <text>
#
# Env: HC (api base), HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY, optional RTC_STATE_ROOT.
set -euo pipefail

HC="${HC:?set HC, e.g. https://hc.example.com}"
KEY="${HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY:?set HEALTHCHECKS_API_KEY}"
STATE_ROOT="${RTC_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.fortress/state}"

cmd="${1:?command}"; repo="${2:?repo}"; task="${3:?task}"
shift 3 2>/dev/null || true

slug="${task//[^a-zA-Z0-9]/-}"
dir="$STATE_ROOT/$repo"; mkdir -p "$dir"
uuid_file="$dir/$task.hcuuid"
ping_file="$dir/$task.ping"

uuid() {
  if [[ -s "$uuid_file" ]]; then cat "$uuid_file"; return; fi
  # recover uuid for an existing check (e.g. claim raced)
  local got
  got=$(curl -sf -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" "$HC/api/v1/checks/$slug/"         | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ping_url"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1])')
  printf '%s' "$got" > "$uuid_file"
  printf '%s' "$got"
}

case "$cmd" in
  claim)
    name="${1:-$task}"
    if ! curl -sf -X POST "$HC/api/v1/checks/" -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY"           --data-urlencode "name=$name"           --data "slug=$slug&timeout=600&grace=600&channels="           | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ping_url"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1])'           > "$uuid_file"; then
      : > "$uuid_file"; uuid > /dev/null   # exists already -> recover uuid
    fi
    curl -sf "$HC/ping/$(cat "$uuid_file")/start" > /dev/null
    touch "$ping_file"
    ;;
  start)
    curl -sf "$HC/ping/$(uuid)/start" > /dev/null; touch "$ping_file" ;;
  ping)
    curl -sf "$HC/ping/$(uuid)" > /dev/null; touch "$ping_file" ;;
  fail)
    curl -sf --data-binary "${1:-failed}" "$HC/ping/$(uuid)/fail" > /dev/null ;;
  log)
    curl -sf --data-binary "$*" "$HC/ping/$(uuid)/log" > /dev/null
    touch "$ping_file" ;;
  *) echo "unknown command: $cmd" >&2; exit 64 ;;

The structure (problem → evidence → process → proof → CTA) is exactly right, and the specificity ("73% bill reduction," "six weeks to production") is the kind of thing buyers actually skim for. ## The tells

**1. Grandiose, unverifiable numbers with no attribution.**
"$1.1M monthly spend removed" / "12 deployments" / "0.3/mo incidents, down from 3" — real consultancies don't lead with this. Unnamed figures at this scale read as marketing copy, not evidence. Buyers discount them to zero.

**2. The punchline-fragment rhythm.**
"Most teams get the demo working. The gap between that and ten thousand requests an hour is the job." This is the LLM's favorite move: a short declarative setup, then a wry aphoristic payoff. Humans in B2B consulting don't write like this — engineers smell it instantly.

**3. Perfectly parallel triads.**
"the routing, the traces, the workload identity and the eval suite." LLMs love balanced fours and threes. Human technical writing is lumpier.

**4. Self-referential signposting.**
"Here's the architecture, including the two failure modes we hit first." / "This is the span structure that makes that possible." Nobody says "here's the X" — they just describe the X.

**5. The knowing-counselor closer.**
"If you're staring at an LLM bill you can't explain, that's usually where the conversation starts." This is a therapist's voice, not a consulting firm's. And "We stay ninety days... then leave you the runbooks and go quiet" is screenplay dialogue.

**6. Absolute claims.**
"Every library here came out of a client's problem." No real business can honestly say *every*. The reader's trust dies on words like this.

**Hero:**

> AI infrastructure consulting for companies running LLM systems in production.

> We build the routing layer, observability stack, workload identity, and evaluation harness that production features need. Most teams can get a demo working. > Written from client engagements.

> **Agentic Routing for Enterprise** (2025) — Most production traffic is classification or extraction that a small model handles at a fraction of the price. **How we work:**

> 01 — **Audit.** We review your existing setup and identify where it will break under load, with an estimate of what it costs you per month today.
> 02 — **Design.** We design against your actual constraints — request volume, latency ceilings, budget — not a reference architecture.

**1. Default browser link styling — the biggest tell.**
In the tooling section, `agentgateway` and `Details →` render as raw blue underlined links. Nothing on a page says "unfinished template" faster than unstyled anchors. These should be ink-colored, no underline, with the arrow doing the work. This one fix costs minutes and removes the cheapest-looking element on the site.

**2. Three typefaces fighting.**
Serif display + monospace labels + sans body. Individually fine, but the serif is doing "tasteful editorial" while the mono is doing "terminal" while the sans is doing "SaaS." Pick a lane: the mono + sans pairing is the right one for an infrastructure firm. Let the serif go, or demote it to headlines only and kill the mono-everywhere pattern.

**3. The royal blue is the default "AI company blue."**
It's essentially Tailwind's blue-600. Every LLM-adjacent brand uses it. A monochrome base (ink/off-white) with one distinctive accent — a desaturated teal, an oxide red, even just a darker ink with blue reserved for interactive states — would immediately separate you from the field. Also: the STABLE/BETA chips are mint green, which isn't in your palette anywhere else. Consistency of accent is what makes a palette feel designed rather than assembled.

**4. The stats band is too loud for its content.**
Giant monospace numbers at maximum contrast for claims that are, as we discussed, your weakest material. The visual hierarchy is screaming the thing the copy should be whispering. Shrink it, move it, or replace it with one sentence and a client name.

**5. Every section is the same card.**
Research card, tool card, case-study card — same thin border, same padding, same rhythm, stacked full-width. There's no visual hierarchy between "our process" and "our tools." Give sections distinct layouts: the demo deserves a terminal-like treatment; case studies could break the grid; the process steps could sit in a two-column layout on desktop. Variety of layout is what reads as "designed" to a scanning engineer.

**6. The logo is the weakest asset.**
The circle-with-a-line mark plus typewriter "Meridian." reads as a placeholder. The trailing period is a nice instinct — keep that idea, but the wordmark and mark need one more design pass. This is the one element a buyer sees on every page and remembers.

**7. The domain mismatch is now visible.**
Your footer says hello@meridian.ai but the site lives on meridian.mumchimp.com. If you own meridian.ai, point the site at it this week — before anything else on this list. If you don't own it, the email is a problem of a different kind.

from typing import List, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class FormalSpec(BaseModel):
    """Tier 1 output: extracted, checkable constraints.

    Invariants/constraints must be machine-checkable assertions where possible.
    Anything that cannot be expressed as an assertion is an ambiguity.
    """
    objective: str
    inputs: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    outputs: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    invariants: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Always-true conditions")
    constraints: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Must-hold requirements")
    ambiguities: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Unresolvable without human input")
    requires_human: bool = Field(default=False, description="True if ambiguities block safe execution")


class VerifiedTaskOutput(BaseModel):
    reasoning_summary: str = ""
    plan_steps: List[str]
    code_implementation: str
    unit_tests: List[str]
    dependencies: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="pip requirements, e.g. ['numpy==1.26.4']")


class SpecEnforcement(str):
    pass


def parse_model(cls, raw: str):
    """Parse model output leniently: full JSON, or first balanced {...} block."""
    import json
    raw = raw.strip()
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        start = raw.find("{")
        end = raw.rfind("}")
        if start == -1 or end <= start:
            raise ValueError("no JSON object found in model output")
        data = json.loads(raw[start:end + 1])
    if hasattr(cls, "model_validate"):
        return cls.model_validate(data)
    return cls.parse_obj(data)

from typing import List, Optional, Protocol
import json


class Router(Protocol):
    def generate(self, messages: list, max_tokens: int = 4096) -> str:
        ...


class LiteLLMRouter:
    """Routes through LiteLLM. Models are an ordered fallback chain — never a single hardcoded provider."""

    def __init__(self, models: List[str], router_kwargs: Optional[dict] = None):
        if not models:
            raise ValueError("at least one model required")
        self.models = list(models)
        self.router_kwargs = router_kwargs or {}

    def generate(self, messages: list, max_tokens: int = 4096) -> str:
        import litellm  # lazy import: engine must work offline too
        last_err = None
        for model in self.models:
            try:
                resp = litellm.completion(
                    model=model,
                    messages=messages,
                    max_tokens=max_tokens,
                    **self.router_kwargs,
                )
                return resp.choices[0].message.content or ""
            except Exception as e:  # provider down / rate limited / context overflow -> next fallback
                last_err = e
        raise RuntimeError(f"all fallback models exhausted: {last_err}")


class FakeRouter:
    """Scripted responses for tests: list of strings yielded in order, last one repeats."""

    def __init__(self, responses: List[str]):
        self._responses = list(responses)
        self._i = 0
        self.calls: List[list] = []

    def generate(self, messages: list, max_tokens: int = 4096) -> str:
        self.calls.append(messages)
        r = self._responses[min(self._i, len(self._responses) - 1)]
        self._i += 1
        return r

class Verdict(str, Enum):
    PASS = "PASS"
    FAIL = "FAIL"               # deterministic failure (assertion/exception/compile)
    TIMEOUT = "TIMEOUT"         # wall-clock exceeded (infinite loop / deadlock suspect)
    OOM = "OOM"                 # memory limit exceeded
    SANDBOX_ERROR = "SANDBOX_ERROR"  # infra problem — NOT a code failure; do not feed back as one


@dataclass
class SandboxResult:
    verdict: Verdict
    stdout: str = ""
    stderr: str = ""
    duration_s: float = 0.0
    notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def error_text(self) -> str:
        return (self.stderr or self.stdout or "").strip()


_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 256 * 1024  # cap captured output: protects memory AND downstream context windows


def _cap(s: str) -> str:
    b = s.encode("utf-8", "replace")
    if len(b) <= _MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES:
        return s
    return b[:_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES].decode("utf-8", "replace") + f"\n...[truncated {len(b) - _MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES} bytes]"


def _classify(returncode: int, stderr: str, oom_hint: bool) -> Verdict:
    if oom_hint or "out of memory" in stderr.lower() or returncode == 137:
        return Verdict.OOM
    if returncode == 0:
        return Verdict.PASS
    return Verdict.FAIL


def build_script(code: str, tests: List[str]) -> str:
    return (
        code
        + "\n\n# --- AUTOMATED TEST SUITE (appended by NSVEE) ---\n"
        + "\n".join(tests)
        + "\n"
    )


class DockerRunner:
    """Hard-isolated execution. Requires docker daemon; image pulled once."""

    def __init__(self, image: str = "python:3.11-slim", cpu_cores: float = 0.5,
                 memory_mb: int = 256, pids_limit: int = 64):
        self.image = image
        self.cpu_cores = cpu_cores
        self.memory_mb = memory_mb
        self.pids_limit = pids_limit

    def available(self) -> bool:
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(["docker", "info"], capture_output=True, timeout=10)
            return r.returncode == 0
        except Exception:
            return False

    def run(self, script: str, timeout_s: int) -> SandboxResult:
        tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="nsvee_")
        path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "main.py")
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(script)
        name = f"nsvee-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
        cmd = [
            "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", name,
            "--network", "none",
            "--memory", f"{self.memory_mb}m",
            "--cpus", str(self.cpu_cores),
            "--pids-limit", str(self.pids_limit),
            "--read-only",
            "--tmpfs", "/tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=16m",
            "--cap-drop", "ALL",
            "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
            "-v", f"{path}:/work/main.py:ro",
            self.image, "python3", "-I", "-B", "/work/main.py",
        ]
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        timed_out = False
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s + 2)
            rc, out, err = r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            timed_out = True
            rc, out, err = -1, "", ""
        finally:
            # belt and suspenders: never leave a container behind
            subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", name],
                           capture_output=True, timeout=10)
            try:
                os.unlink(path); os.rmdir(tmpdir)
            except OSError:
                pass
        dur = time.monotonic() - t0
        if timed_out:
            return SandboxResult(Verdict.TIMEOUT, duration_s=dur,
                                 notes=["exceeded wall-clock budget"])
        return SandboxResult(
            verdict=_classify(rc, err or "", oom_hint=False),
            stdout=_cap(out or ""), stderr=_cap(err or ""), duration_s=dur,
        )


class RlimitsRunner:
    """Fallback for hosts without docker (e.g. local Mac dev loop).

    Weaker isolation: same kernel/user. Scrub env, clamp rlimits, kill the
    whole process group on timeout. Use DockerRunner in any shared/prod estate.
    """

    def __init__(self, memory_mb: int = 256):
        self.memory_mb = memory_mb

    def available(self) -> bool:
        return os.name == "posix"

    def _limits(self):
        resource = _resource
        assert resource is not None, 'rlimits runner requires POSIX'
        cpu = 20  # seconds of CPU
        mem = self.memory_mb * 1024 * 1024
        return [
            (resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (cpu, cpu + 1)),
            (resource.RLIMIT_AS, (mem, mem)),
            (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (8 * 1024 * 1024, 8 * 1024 * 1024)),
            (resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (64, 64)),
            (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (64, 64)),
        ]

    def _apply_limits(self):
        if _resource is None:
            return
        for k, v in self._limits():
            _resource.setrlimit(k, v)

    def run(self, script: str, timeout_s: int) -> SandboxResult:
        env = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "HOME": "/tmp"}
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            p = subprocess.Popen(
                ["python3", "-I", "-B", "-c", script],
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                text=True, env=env, start_new_session=True,
                preexec_fn=self._apply_limits,
            )
            try:
                out, err = p.communicate(timeout=timeout_s)
                rc = p.returncode
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(os.getpgid(p.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
                p.communicate(timeout=5)
                return SandboxResult(Verdict.TIMEOUT, duration_s=time.monotonic() - t0,
                                     notes=["exceeded wall-clock budget; process group killed"])
            return SandboxResult(
                verdict=_classify(rc, err or "", oom_hint=(rc == -9)),
                stdout=_cap(out or ""), stderr=_cap(err or ""), duration_s=time.monotonic() - t0,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            return SandboxResult(Verdict.SANDBOX_ERROR, notes=[f"runner infra error: {e}"])


def default_runner() -> "DockerRunner | RlimitsRunner":
    d = DockerRunner()
    return d if d.available() else RlimitsRunner()
